test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In which of the following places was the Round Table Discussion on improving female workforce participation in India, organised by the Ministry of Labour and Employment and the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, held in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 2, B - 1, C - 4, D - 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Nutrition Plan (2001-02)**: This plan, often referred to under the **National Nutrition Mission**, was initiated in **2001-02**. It was designed to provide **free foodgrains** to **pregnant and lactating women**, **under-nourished children**, and **adolescent girls** belonging to families **below the poverty line (BPL)**. The mission aimed to tackle **malnutrition** and **anemia** at the grassroots level. ***Hence, statement A - 2 is correct.***
 
• **Swajal Dhara Yojana (2002-03)**: Launched by the then Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** in **December 2002** (effective in the **2002-03** fiscal year), this scheme aimed to provide **clean drinking water** to rural areas through **community participation**. It shifted the focus from a **government-led** supply model to a **demand-driven** model. ***Hence, statement B - 1 is correct.***
 
• **Universal Health Insurance Plan (2003-04)**: The **Universal Health Insurance Scheme (UHIS)** was launched in **2003-04** to improve access to **healthcare** for the poor. It provided **subsidized premiums** for individuals and families **below the poverty line**, covering **hospitalization expenses**, **accidental death**, and **loss of wages**. ***Hence, statement C - 4 is correct.***
 
• **Hariyali Project (2003)**: Launched in **January 2003**, the **Hariyali Project** was a massive **watershed development** program. It was implemented through **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** to empower local communities in **rainwater harvesting**, **afforestation**, and **soil conservation**. ***Hence, statement D - 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Watershed Management in India**: The **Hariyali Project** integrated several existing programs like the **Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP)**, the **Desert Development Programme (DDP)**, and the **Integrated Wastelands Development Programme (IWDP)**. Its primary objective was to ensure **ecological balance** and **sustainable livelihoods** for the rural population by managing **land, water, and biomass**.
 
• **Rural Water Supply Evolution**: **Swajal Dhara** was a landmark because it required the **beneficiary community** to contribute **10%** of the **capital cost** of the project, while the **Central Government** provided the remaining **90%**. This ensured that the **local community** took **ownership** and responsibility for the **operation and maintenance** of the water assets.
 
• **Health Security for the Vulnerable**: The **Universal Health Insurance Scheme** originally offered a **subsidy** of **Rs. 200** for an individual, **Rs. 300** for a family of five, and **Rs. 400** for a family of seven. It served as a precursor to more expansive schemes like **Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY)** and the current **Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY)**.
 
• **Nutrition Interventions**: The **National Nutrition Plan** targeted **51** nutritionally deficient districts in its pilot phase. It focused specifically on **adolescent girls** weighing less than **35 kg** to ensure they received **6 kg** of **free foodgrains** per month through the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Framework**: Most of these schemes during the early **2000s** emphasized **decentralization**. For instance, the **Hariyali guidelines** made the **Gram Panchayat** the implementation agency, while the **Zilla Parishad** or **District Rural Development Agency (DRDA)** acted as the **nodal authority** at the district level.
 
• **Linguistic and Regional Reach**: These schemes were implemented across all **States and Union Territories** of **India**, catering to diverse **climatic zones** (in the case of **Hariyali**) and **socio-economic** strata (in the case of **UHIS** and **Nutrition Plan**).
 
• **Yearly Significance**: The period between **2001 and 2004** marked a significant era in **Indian social policy**, moving towards **participatory governance** and **targeted subsidies** for **BPL families**.
</ul
